protein: SHP2 (PTPN11), a multi-domain non-receptor tyrosine phosphatase; full-length construct
readout: Enrichment score in a yeast growth-rescue assay, relative to wild-type full-length SHP2
assay_method: A yeast (S. cerevisiae) growth-rescue assay: an active tyrosine kinase (v-Src or kinase-dead c-Src) arrests yeast growth, and co-expressed SHP2 phosphatase activity rescues it. Saturation-mutagenesis libraries, built by the MITE tiling method, were selected for 24 h outgrowth; variant abundance before and after selection was deep-sequenced and reduced to an enrichment score relative to wild-type SHP2. Two to four replicates per variant.
remark: The reference sequence is UniProt Q06124 (human PTPN11/SHP2), 593 residues, unmodified; all 10,899 missense labels verify against it exactly. There is no synthesized WT row: the tiling library carries 593 synonymous (WT-to-WT) codon variants, one per position, and their mean is used, which reads as exactly 0 because the enrichment score is itself defined relative to wild type. A parallel "stop" category at every position is dropped, being unrepresentable in the four-column format. 368 further cells across the workbook have no computable enrichment value (a missing replicate or a variant absent from the library) and are dropped. The paper's abstract states "over 11,000 SHP2 mutants" across both constructs combined; this branch's two datasets total 16,181 because SHP2 PTP's 289 positions all fall inside SHP2 FL's 593, so most PTP-domain mutations are measured -- as genuinely separate molecules, under a separate selection -- in both datasets. The FL count alone, 10,899, is the closer match to the paper's figure; the union of the two libraries' distinct (position, substitution) pairs (before this branch's domain-relative renumbering of PTP) is also close to that, since PTP contributes very few positions FL does not already cover. Neither reading forces an exact match, and none was attempted. Not extracted from this paper: the Supplementary Data 3 "Clinical Variants" sheet, which is a 595-row cross-reference of this same enrichment data against ClinVar and COSMIC entries rather than an independent measurement; the COSMIC- and ClinVar-annotated sheets, which carry no enrichment scores at all; and the molecular-dynamics and structural analyses, which are computational.
